title: Common transversal of left and right cosets (P. Hall)
statement: Let $H$ be a finite group and let $K \le H$ be a subgroup. Then there exist a natural number $n$ and elements $h_1, \dots, h_n \in H$ such that the assignment $i \mapsto h_i K$, sending each index to the corresponding left coset viewed as a subset of $H$, is a bijection from $\{1, \dots, n\}$ onto the collection of all subsets of $H$, and, simultaneously, the assignment $i \mapsto K h_i$, sending each index to the corresponding right coset, is also a bijection from $\{1, \dots, n\}$ onto the collection of all subsets of $H$.
caveat: The Lean gives the two coset maps codomain `Set H` (all subsets of $H$), so `Function.Bijective` literally asserts each map is a bijection onto the full power set of $H$ — which is what I rendered. This is almost certainly a mis-formalization of the classical P. Hall result (where the maps should enumerate exactly the left, resp. right, cosets of $K$); read literally the formal claim is false, but per the ground-truth rule I have stated the formal statement rather than the intended one. Confidence marked low because of this codomain discrepancy.

Ex 5.2.9: a common transversal of the left and right cosets of a subgroup (P. Hall).

5.2.9 Let $H$ be a finite group and let $K$ be a subgroup of $H$. Show that there exist
elements $h_1, h_2, \ldots, h_n \in H$ such that $h_1K, h_2K, \ldots, h_nK$ are the left
cosets of $K$ and $Kh_1, Kh_2, \ldots, Kh_n$ are the right cosets of $K$. (P. Hall)
